title: The Al Davis Collection
subtitle: Coach. Commissioner. Owner-leader. Architect of the Raiders.
summary: A source-backed collection of turning points in Al Davis' Raiders story: the 1963 turnaround, the AFL commissioner era, championships, relocation battles, landmark leadership decisions, Hall of Fame induction, the return to Oakland, and the end of a half-century leading the franchise.

milestones.title: Head coach and general manager
milestones.summary: Al Davis was named Raiders head coach and general manager. Oakland finished 10-4 that season for the first winning record in franchise history.

milestones.title: AFL commissioner
milestones.summary: Davis left Oakland to become the second commissioner of the American Football League. The AFL and NFL announced their alliance on June 8; Davis resigned as commissioner on July 25 and returned to the Raiders as Managing General Partner.

milestones.title: First Super Bowl title and Executive of the Year
milestones.summary: After the Raiders defeated Minnesota 32-14 in Super Bowl XI on January 9, Davis was named NFL Executive of the Year on March 5.

milestones.title: Super Bowl XV
milestones.summary: The Raiders defeated Philadelphia 27-10 in Super Bowl XV, securing the franchise's second Super Bowl championship during Davis' leadership.

milestones.title: The Los Angeles move cleared in court
milestones.summary: A federal jury found for the Raiders and against the NFL in the relocation case, setting up the move to Los Angeles. The Los Angeles Raiders played their first home preseason game at the L.A. Coliseum on August 29.

milestones.title: Super Bowl XVIII
milestones.summary: The Los Angeles Raiders defeated Washington 38-9 in Super Bowl XVIII, giving the franchise its third Super Bowl title.

milestones.title: Art Shell named head coach
milestones.summary: Davis promoted Hall of Fame tackle Art Shell to head coach. Shell became the first African-American head coach in the modern era of professional football.

milestones.title: Pro Football Hall of Fame
milestones.summary: Davis was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio, with former Raiders head coach John Madden presenting him.
milestones.sourceLabel: Las Vegas Raiders · Hall of Fame

milestones.title: Return to Oakland
milestones.summary: A letter of intent between the Raiders and the Oakland Coliseum was signed on June 23. The agreement followed on August 7, and the Raiders played their first home preseason game back in Oakland on August 12.

milestones.title: A half-century of Raiders leadership ends
milestones.summary: Al Davis died at age 81 after leading the Raiders for roughly half a century. The next day, the Raiders defeated Houston 25-20 in their first game without him.
